plugins.name: Runbooks
plugins.description: Runbooks an agent proposes and a person runs, one approved command at a time, with every output kept.
plugins.author: Coolroo
features: Agents propose runbooks through a token API or MCP; they can never run anything
Each agent token is limited to the hosts you choose for it
A person runs each step after seeing the exact command and host
Run over SSH or send the command to an open terminal and paste the output back
Every run is kept, and a repeat of the same command asks first
Values with {{name}} placeholders in commands and step text, filled by the author or captured from output
Outputs can be hidden from agents step by step
Standard input from an earlier step's output, a value or a secret
Secrets captured from output and kept in OpenBao through the OpenBao Secrets plugin, never shown
Agent steps: work the agent does itself between the person's steps, ended through the API
Runbook events an agent can read or get as a signed webhook, off by default
Send to agent on any step, with a short note
Steps run outside Termix: the command with a Copy button, the pasted output checked
Amendments: an agent fixes a step or adds one after it in place (3a), and later steps keep their numbers
Step kinds: each step shows who does it and how, with its own color, icon and label; the colors can be changed
A bar that goes to the next step (or press N) and a rail of the steps near you, for long runbooks
VM steps: one button starts, shuts down, restarts or shows a VM through HAW VM Manager, as the person who presses it
Sequences: one Run runs commands, delays, waits and wait events (container, unit, log, http, port, file, job) in order, with no sleep
Send to terminal fills the Mark done box with the command's output, for the person to check and save
A list in Open, Done and Abandoned sections with folders inside, each collapsible and remembered for each person, and a search over titles

gated.notes:
### Fixed

- **Send to terminal fills the Mark done box with bash 5.3** (BUG-024). On Enter, bash 5.3 draws a pasted command of one row again by a carriage return and a move right past the prompt. The reading started its copy of the row at the left edge, so the command did not match there, and the box stayed the empty paste box. This happened whenever the prompt and the command fit on one row: on a PC always, on a phone when the screen is wide enough. The reading now starts after the noted prompt and a space, as the terminal shows it. A command that wraps worked before and still works. Tests replay bash 5.3.9 recorded on home-server at 80, 54 and 40 columns.

One release for the work planned as 1.4.9 (output read from the terminal), sequences with waits and wait events, and folders in the list. 1.4.9 was never released.

### Added

- **Sequences** (T-034). A step that Termix runs on a host may be a `sequence` of 1 to 20 items instead of one command: `run` items (a command with its own `label`, `checks`, `captures`, `timeoutMs`, `interactive` and `onFail`), `delay` items (1 to 3600 seconds, with a `reason`; a timer in Termix, nothing runs on the host) and the waits below. One **Run** runs the items in order as the person who pressed it, also with the page closed. The step card lists each item with its state (waiting, running, passed, failed, skipped), its time, its live output and a delay's countdown with **Skip**. A failed item stops the sequence and fails the step, unless it has `"onFail": "continue"`. **Stop** ends the item that runs; after a stop, a failure or a Termix restart, **Continue from item N** starts a new run that keeps the items that passed (409 `changed` when the sequence or its values changed). Before each item after the first, Runbooks checks that the person may still connect to the host. A step's `workdir` (an absolute path) runs every run item as `cd -- '<workdir>' && <command>`, and works on a one-command step too. An item's captures fill `{{name}}` in the items after it. Each run of a sequence step has `items`, one record per item; agents get one `step-done` or `step-failed` event for the step, not one per item. Not on a sequence step: `stdin`, `secretCaptures`, `where`, `owner: "agent"`, `runIn: "terminal"` (Send to terminal is refused). REST and MCP take and show sequences; a hidden step hides each item's output, captures and error. Migration 0021.
- **Wait items and retry** (T-036). A `wait` item runs a command until its checks pass, on a schedule: `within` (required, up to 7200 seconds), `attempts` (up to 500), `every` (default 5 s), `backoff` (`fixed`, `linear`, `exponential` with `factor`), `maxDelay`, `jitter` (`none`, `full`, `equal`) and `stopIf` checks that fail it at once. A `run` item's `retry` runs a flaky command again on the same schedule, with `retryOn` (`exit`, `check`, `timeout`, `connect`). The card shows the planned schedule ("up to 120 attempts, every 30 s, at most 1 h"), which the person approves with the commands, then attempt dots, the attempt counter, a countdown with **Try now** and the earlier attempts folded. One Run press covers every attempt: attempts never ask the repeat question. Each attempt is kept (`attempts` on the item, with `why` it did not pass); the step has `attempt` and `schedules` for agents. An attempt's output is read on its own (`GET .../runs/{runId}/items/{item}/attempts/{attempt}`, MCP `get_attempt`). A Termix restart fails the waiting item as interrupted; Continue starts it again. Migration 0022 (`run_attempts`).
- **Wait events** (T-038): items that wait until a state holds, checked by Termix itself, on the wait schedule, with no loop, `grep` or `test` on the host. `container` (`healthy`, `running`, `exited`, `gone`; one fixed `docker container inspect`), `unit` (`active`, or `finished` with `Result=success` since the step started; one fixed `systemctl show`), `log` (a line in a container's log or a unit's journal, written after the step started, matches `pattern`, or `failPattern` fails it), `http` (status and text of an address), `port` (`open` or `closed` on the host's loopback), `file` (`exists`, `nonEmpty`, `gone`, over SFTP; `sudo: true` for one fixed `sudo -n stat`) and `job` (a long command started with `sudo -n systemd-run` as a transient unit, followed to its end with its journal streamed, then unloaded; past the 10-minute limit of one command). Each check is an attempt whose `result` says the state in fixed words (`healthy`, `exited (1)`, `port closed`, `HTTP 503`, `forwarding refused`). A state that cannot turn good (a container that exited or restarted, a failed unit, permission denied) fails the item at once. Names, paths, units and URLs are checked when written and go into the fixed commands quoted after `--`. Linux-only events are refused (400 `linux-only`) for a host tagged `windows` and fail at once on a host whose SSH server says it is Windows. The card shows each event's icon, what it checks, its attempt dots and the last state. Migration 0023 (the attempt's `result`).
- `port`, and `http` to the host's own loopback (`127.0.0.1` or `localhost`), open a TCP channel from the host through the SSH connection, always to the literal `127.0.0.1` (the URL keeps `localhost` for the `Host` header and the certificate). The host's SSH key needs `permitopen="127.0.0.1:*"` and `permitlisten="127.0.0.1:1"` instead of `no-port-forwarding`; a refused channel fails the item at once with words that say so, never as a closed port. `::1` (`[::1]` in a URL) is refused when written: "write 127.0.0.1; Termix's SSH key allows forwarding to 127.0.0.1 only". Any other `http` URL must be `https://` and goes from Termix through core's `ctx.fetch`, with no redirects followed; the certificate is always checked.
- **Admin setting: Extra trusted CAs for http checks (PEM)** (`httpCaPem`). CA certificates, such as a home CA, that `http` items trust besides the public roots. Only Runbooks' http checks use them.
- **No sleep in commands** (T-034, owner's rule 2026-11-19). Runbooks refuses a command that waits a fixed time when a runbook is created, steps are added, a step changes or is amended: 400 with `code` `sleep` and a message that points to the `delay`, `wait` and event items. It reads `sleep` as the shell reads the word (`sleep -- 5`, `sleep${IFS}5`, `s''leep 5`, `time.sleep(5)`), `Start-Sleep`, `timeout /t`, `read -t <n>`, `timeout <n>` before a command that never ends, and `ping -n`/`-c` used as a delay; also in wait and job commands, and in values once filled (a Run whose values make a command wait is refused). Steps stored before keep running. **Admin setting: Refuse sleep in commands** (`banSleep`), on by default.
- **Captured values need a pattern** (BUG-022 M3, owner's choice 2026-11-23). A value captured from output may go into a later command, an event's name, path or URL only when what captures it has a `value` check with `matches`; otherwise the change is refused with 400 `captured-value`. At run time the value must match that pattern as a whole, or the item that uses it fails before it runs.
- **Folders, sections and search in the list** (T-040). The Runbooks list has three sections, **Open**, **Done** and **Abandoned**, each with its count; Open starts expanded, the others collapsed. Inside each, runbooks are grouped by folder, A to Z, with **No folder** last, each folder with its count. Each person's collapsed sections and folders are kept on the server (a hidden per-user setting, `listCollapsed`). A search box keeps the runbooks whose title has every word typed. **Move to folder** on each row and on the runbook page, and **Rename** on a folder row, work on any status, change nothing else, and are in Termix's audit log. A folder is one level: 1 to 60 characters, no `/`; a name that is an existing folder in other letters gets its spelling. Agents set `folder` on create and `PATCH` (REST and MCP; a `PATCH` with only `folder` changes no status, revision or event) and list one folder with `GET /runbooks?folder=...` or `list_runbooks`. Migration 0024 (`runbooks.folder`).
- **Send to terminal fills the Mark done box with its own output** (T-249). The person no longer copies the output from the terminal, which a phone cannot do. Once the person presses Enter in the terminal, the **Mark done** box fills with what the command prints, and follows the terminal until the person changes the text. It only fills the box: a line above it always says "Check the text before you save it" (or "The terminal waits for a password"), and it never says the command finished (BUG-021, owner's choice 2026-11-23: guessing where the output ends is what kept failing). **Read again** reads the terminal again and puts its text back after a change. The person still sees, can change, and presses **Mark done** or **Mark failed**. The toast after Send to terminal says the output comes back to the step.
- It reads SSH Terminal's handle on the terminal tab (`readBufferLines`, `subscribeOutput`, `getInputModes`, `isAtPasswordPrompt`), which the plugin SDK does not declare: every part is tested before use and never throws. Without it (a Termix that changes it, plugin API 2's frames, a page reload, another device), the box is the empty paste box it was. The screen is read once, before the command is typed, to note the prompt; the text comes only from the raw output after that (BUG-019, BUG-021), so a reflow, a full scrollback, `clear` or tmux cannot bring another run's text in. The text starts only after the command's echo: the line the shell ends on Enter must be the noted prompt's end with the command (bash 5.1+ draws a pasted command again on Enter, a long or multi-line one after moving the cursor up; that redraw is followed). When the echo is not the command (the person changed it), or cannot be followed, nothing is read and the person pastes. The reading stops at the next prompt (where the shell turns line editing on again, `ESC[?2004h`, which bash 5.1+, zsh and fish send, so a prompt that `cd` changed still ends it; or, for other shells, the prompt noted before the send at the start of a line, if it is 3 characters or more), at a cursor move to another row (`clear`, a progress display, tmux; a note says the end may be missing), at Mark done's size limit (256 K characters) or at the time limit (an hour, or the step's longer one). Lines that look like a prompt (`# ` in a config file, a progress bar ending in `% `) never end it. What the person runs after is never read. While nothing new comes, the box reads every 5 seconds, and it stops reading once the reading stopped. No reading starts when the terminal's last line does not look like a prompt (a tmux status line, a MOTD still printing). A reading stops where it is when another Send to terminal types into the same terminal or its tab closes, and ends when the run is done or failed on another device or reopened; up to 20 are kept. Tests play bash 5.2 output recorded in a terminal (a read before the echo, a changed command, `clear`, a root prompt with `cat` of a config file, a command of two lines, a pause after a progress bar, a command typed ahead after `cd`, a long command redrawn on Enter, a two-line prompt) on the real terminal library (`@xterm/xterm` 6.0.0, a dev dependency).
- A run's `outputSource` says where its pasted output came from: `pasted`, `captured` (from the terminal, as read) or `captured-edited`. `POST /runs/{id}/complete` takes it (default `pasted`; 400 for another value); a run with no pasted output has `null`, as do runs from before. The run shows "Output read from the terminal" or "…, then changed" for it; agents read it on every run, and `null` on a hidden step, since whether it printed anything is its output too (BUG-019). It is what the page reports, not proof that the text was not typed by hand. Captured text is the run's `pastedOutput`, so secret masking, checks, captures and secret captures read it as they read a paste. docs/agent-api.md has a section "Output read from the terminal", and docs/security.md says what is read and what is not (no-echo input never reaches the screen; echoed text is read like any output).
- **Mark failed** sends the text read from the terminal only if the person opened (clicked or tapped into) or changed the box; otherwise it sends no output, as in 1.4.8 (BUG-019, owner's choice 2026-11-23). A line under the buttons says so. **Mark done** is unchanged.
- New column `runs.output_source` (migration 0020), for SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL.

### Changed

- The latest run's Mark done box starts empty for each new run; it kept the text typed for the run before.
- The Run confirm of a sequence shows each item's checks, `stopIf`, capture patterns, `onFail: "continue"`, `interactive`, schedule and what each event checks (BUG-022 L3). The card shows capture patterns.

### Security

- From the security review of sequences, waits and events before release (BUG-022): a `log` item's `pattern` and `failPattern` run with a time limit (250 ms for all new lines of one check): a pattern that backtracks without end fails the item with `pattern too slow`, and Termix goes on. A repeated group that holds a repeat or alternatives, at any depth (`(a+)+`, `((a+))+`, `(a|aa)+`), is refused when written (H1).
- A `job`'s journal is redacted (secrets, hidden typed input) before it is shown live, stored or read by agents (H2). Every event's text is redacted the same way (L4).
- An event item that reads a hidden value hides its step from agents, as a command does (M1).
- Stored output is capped: an item's last attempt keeps its whole output (256 KB per stream), an earlier attempt the last 4 KB of each stream, an item's earlier attempts 256 KB together, and a run 8 MB (M2).
- `http` items never reach Termix's own loopback, its own addresses, unspecified, link-local or reserved addresses, in any spelling (IPv4 in decimal, octal or hex, IPv4-mapped, compatible, translated and NAT64 forms): such an address in a URL is refused when written, and a name that resolves to one fails the item (`address refused`). Only a private address that is not loopback gets core's `allowPrivateHosts` (M4). DNS rebinding through a private name stays possible: docs/security.md says what that leaves.
- **Try now** and **Skip** need the person who pressed Run, or a person who may connect to the step's host (403 `not-your-run`) (L2). A `file` item's result does not say the file's size (L1). A **Stop**, or the time limit, while `systemd-run` starts a job stops its unit too (L5).

### Fixed

- **A VM step's card no longer shows an old read.** The card read its VM only when it opened and when its own step ran, so a VM that an earlier step made or changed still showed as not found, and the button stayed off until the person found **Read again**. The card now reads the VM again when a run of any step of the runbook ends, and when the page shows again after a minute or more; one read runs at a time. **Read again** is an outline button with an icon next to the VM's state, and the card says how old the read is ("read 3 min ago"). A failed read, or a VM HAW cannot act on now, shows in a box with the time of the read, a line that an earlier step may have made or changed the VM, and **Read again**. The action button stays as it was after a failed read: pressing it asks HAW again.

### Added

- **VM steps.** A step's `vm: { host, name, action, force?, waitFor?, waitSeconds?, value? }` gives the person one button, and HAW VM Manager (1.0.3 or later, through its service `haw.vms`) does the action on that VM as the person who pressed it, with HAW's roles and the host's own limits (name pattern, protect list, ceilings). `action` is `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `show` or `console`. HAW keeps each action in its record with "via runbooks: runbook 12 step 3". An admin adds `runbooks` to HAW's **Plugins that may act for a person** first; until then, and without HAW, the step says why it cannot run.
- The step waits for `waitFor` (by default the state the action leads to: `running` for start and restart, `off` for stop; none for show; `null` for no wait), reading the VM every 2 seconds for up to `waitSeconds` (1 to 600, default 300), and fails at the limit with the last state. When HAW restarts or updates during a wait, the step says "HAW VM Manager did not answer; it may be restarting" and goes on to its time limit; Runbooks binds to HAW again only on HAW's code `bad-key`, and steps that wait at once never clear each other's key. Its run, in mode `vm`, shows each state as it changes, and ends with the VM's details as JSON and one summary line ("wyatt-pc-builder is running, 192.0.2.10"), which checks (`contains`, `notContains`, `matches`, `notMatches`) and `when` output rules read. `value: "build"` sets `{{build.state}}`, `{{build.id}}` and, when the VM has an address, `{{build.ip}}` (the first IPv4 address, else the first) and `{{build.addresses}}` for later steps.
- The card shows the host, the VM, its state now (HAW's `show`, read when the card opens, `GET /steps/{id}/vm`), what the action does and how long it waits, and "the host refuses this" for a protected VM's stop or restart and for a VM outside the host's name pattern. The button names the action: **Start VM**, **Shut down VM**, **Restart VM**, **Show VM**, **Open console**; with `force`, **Turn off VM** or **Reset VM** in red, with a question of its own (409 `force`, then `confirmForce: true`). `POST /steps/{id}/vm` keeps the usual questions: the revision, the order, the wait timer, the `when` rule and the repeat guard (the same action on the same VM in the last 24 hours; not for show and console). Two steps with the same power action on the same VM, pressed at once, do not both pass it: the second gets 409 `running` until the first run is written, and then 409 `repeat`. A host whose verbs HAW has not read yet refuses every action (409 `verbs-unknown`). A host's refusal fails the step with HAW's words; HAW's own refusals (Runbooks not allowed, the person's HAW role, a host HAW does not manage or whose `vmctl` does not offer the verb) refuse the button with 403, 404 or 409 and run nothing. **Stop** ends a wait.
- **Open console** opens the VM's console host in a Remote Desktop tab, as HAW's own tab does, and the step waits for the person's **Done** or **Failed** (`POST /steps/{id}/vm/end`). Its run keeps one summary line, not HAW's console details (the console's address and the VM's id).
- A new step kind, **VM action** (indigo, Server), with its own color setting.
- Agents: `vm` on create, add, change and amend, through REST and MCP, and in `get_runbook`. A VM step has no `hostId`, `command`, `captures`, `secretCaptures`, `stdin`, `timeoutMs` or `interactive` and cannot be an agent step (400); `force` is for stop and restart only; `host` must be one of the token's hosts and, when HAW can say, one HAW manages. `GET /vms` and the MCP tool `list_vms` answer the token's VM hosts and the VMs on one from a copy Runbooks reads from HAW, as the signed-in person and marked for an agent, when that person makes the token or saves its hosts; the copy has the time it was read and no VM state, and a token saves without it when HAW is not there or refuses. An agent request never reaches HAW (it has no acting user), and Runbooks never acts as another user: it does not ask for `users:impersonate`. Agents never act on a VM. `hideOutputFromAgents` works on a VM step, and the built agent view test has a VM case and one that changes only the state. A hidden VM step's `{{build.state}}` is one of a few words, so it is not masked in other text (nor is a Decision's option id): whether "running" came back masked would tell the state. A step whose command, checks or standard input reads such a value is hidden from agents instead, and so are the values it captures and the steps that read those. The agent API doc has a section "VM steps"; docs/security.md says what a VM step lets a person do.
- New column `steps.vm` (migration 0019), for SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL. The manifest declares `haw.vms` (`^1.0.0`) as an optional requirement.

### Fixed

- **Interactive steps on Windows hosts.** Windows (ConPTY) paints every row of the terminal empty before the first text, so an interactive run's output started with 39 empty lines; the output now drops empty lines before the first text, in the live output and in the stored output alike. This holds for every host's terminal output, Linux too: an interactive run on Linux no longer starts with the empty lines a program printed first. The agent API doc's "Typed input" says that under a terminal a Windows host may report exit code 0 (wyatt-pc did for `exit 7`), so such a step checks its output instead of its exit code, and that **End input** (Ctrl-D) may not end the input there. How Runbooks reads the exit code does not change: Linux hosts give real exit codes under a terminal.

### Added

- **Run or Send to terminal.** A step's `runIn` says how the person may start its command: `"either"` (the default, as before), `"terminal"` (Send to terminal only) or `"run"` (Run only), with an optional one-line `runInReason`. The step card shows only the button the step allows, with a line that says why ("Send to terminal only: it opens your browser."), and a terminal-only step's chip says "Terminal on <host>" instead of "Run on <host>". The server refuses Run on a terminal-only step with 409 `terminal-only` and Send to terminal on a Run-only step with 409 `run-only`, before it asks about the order, the wait or a repeat; the answer carries `reason`.
- `runIn` and `runInReason` work when an agent creates a runbook, adds, changes or amends a step, through REST and MCP, and show in `get_runbook`. Only a step Termix runs on a host may set them (400 otherwise), and `"terminal"` cannot have `stdin` (400). Older steps read as `"either"`. The agent API doc has a section "Run or Send to terminal".
- **Conditional steps.** A step's `when` rule says when it is needed, from earlier steps only: how a step ended (`{ "step": 8, "status": "failed" }`, also `done`, `skipped`, `ran` and `not-needed`), what its latest run printed (`{ "step": 1, "output": <any check> }`, with `{{name}}` values and secrets hidden), what a decision step chose (`{ "step": 5, "chose": "rollback" }`), or a value (`{ "value": "mode", "equals": "fast" }` or `matches`), combined with `all`, `any` and `not` (at most 4 levels and 20 rules). Steps are written as `3` or `"3a"`, as in `stdin`. A rule that names this step, a later step, a capture the step does not have, or an option a decision does not have is refused with 400. It works when an agent creates a runbook, adds, changes or amends a step, through REST and MCP.
- Runbooks works out each rule's state every time it reads the runbook (`waiting`, `met` or `not-met`) and never stores it, so reopening an earlier step changes the answer. Each step has `condition: { state, rule, reason, notNeeded }`; the reason never quotes output. A pending step that never ran and whose rule does not hold is **not needed**: it counts as ended for the order of later steps, the next step, the bar and the rail, the progress (`notNeeded`, and "2/5 done · 1 not needed"), the list's next kind and `agent-turn`. A step that ran keeps its result. A step that is not needed is not "the step before" for a wait timer: `waitAfterPreviousSeconds` counts from the last step before it that ended.
- A rule reads the author's values and what steps **before** it captured, also for `{{name}}` in an output rule, so a later step that captures the same name cannot change it. A rule that names a step an amendment replaced reads its latest replacement. An output rule on a decision step reads the chosen ids, one per line; a decision that is skipped, or reopened and not chosen again, has no output, no `value` and matches no `chose` rule. A step a rule names cannot be removed (409 `when`) or moved after the rule (400). A change to a step's `captures`, `decision` or `interactive`, and an amendment that replaces a step, check again every rule that reads the step and answer 409 `when` when one no longer fits.
- **A rule never reads hidden output.** Every rule, whoever wrote it, is worked out on what the agent view shows: a hidden step's output and captures read `[hidden by owner]`, a hidden value is masked in other steps' output and captures, and `{{name}}` is filled with the masked value. So a rule's state, `nextStepId`, the progress, `agent-turn` and an agent's 409s are the same whatever the hidden values are. To branch on hidden output, give the hidden step a check and the later step a status rule; on the page, a rule that reads hidden output says "This rule can't see hidden output". An agent's rule that reads a hidden step's output, a value such a step captures, or such a value as `{{name}}` is refused with 400 as an early error.
- Rules are cheap to read. What a pattern said of a finished run or a value is kept for the server's life (1000 answers for each of the 50 runbooks read last), so a page load or a list poll tests no pattern twice. The patterns of one read, or of one list of runbooks, share a limit of 500 ms; a rule whose pattern that limit stopped is `waiting` ("not worked out yet") until a later read, and no `agent-turn` is sent while the turn is not known.
- On the page, a step that is not needed is one grey line in its place, "3 · Way back — not needed: step 1 is done and step 2 is done"; a click opens it. A step whose rule still waits says "Only if step 1 failed or step 2 failed". **Hide not needed** leaves them out of the cards, the rail and the bar, and the browser remembers it.
- A person can still start a step that is not needed: Run, Send to terminal, Make it or Save and Done or Failed answer 409 `not-needed` with the rule and the reason, the page asks **Run anyway?**, and a start after a yes (`conditionAnyway: true`) is in the audit log, written only once every other question passed. An agent cannot complete its own step when it is not needed (409 `not-needed`). The agent API doc has a section "Conditional steps", and its events section says how `agent-turn` treats a step that is not needed.
- **Decision steps.** A step with `decision: { options, multiple?, min?, max?, value? }` lets the person choose from 2 to 10 options the author wrote (`id`, one-line `label`, optional short Markdown `description`), with radio cards or, with `multiple`, check boxes from `min` to `max`. There is no free text. **Confirm** (`POST /steps/{id}/decide`) ends the step done with a run in mode `decision` whose output is the chosen ids, one per line, and sets `value`, when given, to the ids joined with commas. The card then says "You chose: Go back to the old release", by whom and when. A decision step has no host, command, checks, captures, stdin or wait timer, cannot be hidden from agents (400; the page offers no Hide on it), and only a person decides (`owner: "agent"` is refused).
- **Reopen** on a decision lets the person choose again. When steps that read it already ran, the page names them first ("Choose again?"); they stay as history, and steps that have not run follow the new choice (`decisionRan` on the step).
- The agent view shows `decision` and `choice`; `step-done` carries "chose <ids>" as its note. A new step kind, **Decide** (amber, Split), with its own color setting. The agent API doc has a section "Decision steps".
- **Typed input.** While a Run runs, the person who started it can type into the command from the runbook page: a line under the live output, "Type into the command", with **Send** (Enter), **End input** and an eye to hide what they type. It shows on every Run without `stdin` and shows the time left of the step's limit. It lights up and starts hidden when the last line of the output looks like a prompt for a password, passphrase, token or PIN. Another person sees who can type instead. On a phone, Send and End input wrap under the field.
- `POST /runs/{id}/input` with `{ text, hidden?, end? }` writes to the command's standard input. Only the person who started the run (403 `not-your-run`); never a Termix API key or an agent. 409 `not-running`, `stdin-source` (the run got `stdin`) and `input-closed` (input ended); at most 4 KB at once (400 `too-long`). - Live output. Run answers at once and the command goes on in the background. While it runs, the step shows its standard output and standard error as they arrive, how long it has run, and how long since it last printed anything, which turns to a warning after 30 seconds without output. The page reads it every second while a command of the open runbook runs.
- Stop on a running step, after a confirm. It sends the command a TERM signal where the server takes one and closes its session; the run ends failed with "stopped by" and the person, and is audited. Agents and Termix API keys cannot stop a run.
- Agents read a running run's output so far: `running: true`, `stdout` and `stderr` up to now, and `lastOutputAt`, in the agent API and MCP `get_runbook`. Hidden steps still read `[hidden by owner]`.
- Checks on a step's output. Agents set `checks` on a step: `exitCode`, `contains` and `notContains`, `matches` and `notMatches` (on stdout, stderr or either), and `value` (a value the step captures). Runbooks tests them when a run ends, and on the pasted output when a terminal run is marked done. A failed check marks the step failed even on exit code 0; the step lists its checks with a tick or a cross and a reason, and the Run confirm shows them. Runs carry the results as `checks` in the agent API and MCP.
- An optional exit code box next to Mark done for a terminal run.
- Wait timers. Agents set `waitAfterPreviousSeconds` (1 to 86400) and an optional `waitReason` on a step. Once the step before it ends, the step counts down ("Wait 1:42 before you start") and Run and Send to terminal look not-yet; starting before the end asks "Start anyway?" and is audited. The server refuses an early start with 409 `wait` until confirmed. Agents read `waitUntil` on a step while its timer runs.
- Output of a running command is saved every 2 seconds. A run that was running when Termix restarted ends failed with "interrupted: Termix restarted while it ran" and keeps the output saved so far.

### Fixed

- A character split across two pieces of command output (such as an accented letter or a box-drawing line) no longer shows as broken characters.

### Added

- Links that open a runbook: `<Termix address>/?view=runbook&id=<id>` opens the Runbooks tab on that runbook, after a sign-in when the person was signed out. Every runbook in the agent API and MCP answers carries its `openPath`, and the MCP tools tell agents to give the person that link.

### Fixed

- Send to terminal takes one click. With no terminal open to the step's host, it opens one, waits for it to connect and types the command in, instead of only opening it. The "Send to ...?" question is gone: the command is typed without Enter, so nothing runs until you press Enter there. The repeat and order questions stay.
- Send to terminal finds an open terminal when the terminal and Termix give the host id in different forms (text or number), prefers the one on screen, and brings it to the front.
- When a new terminal does not connect within 30 seconds, no run is recorded and Runbooks says to copy the command instead.
- Remote desktop hosts (RDP, VNC, consoles) are no longer offered for agent tokens. Runbooks runs and types commands over SSH only, so token hosts, agent steps, Run and Send to terminal now refuse a host that does not take SSH.
- A 1.0.0 token that lists a remote desktop host stops offering it to agents once someone with Manage Runbooks tokens opens Agent tokens.

### Added

- Runbooks, steps, runs and agent tokens, with migrations for SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL
- An agent API under /plugin-api/runbooks/agent/ and an MCP endpoint, both behind Runbooks tokens; agents propose and read, never run
- Agent tokens limited to the hosts chosen for each token
- Runs over SSH or through an open terminal, with checks for a changed step, step order, repeats and a stored host key
- Values with {{name}} placeholders, filled by the author or captured from output
- Output hidden from agents per step
- A Runbooks tab with the runbook list, step cards, run history, notes and token management

plugins.name: Hundred Acre Wood
plugins.description: A VM manager for any host you add: see every VM, start, stop and restart them, and open their consoles, through one fixed command on each host.
plugins.author: Coolroo
features: Add any Termix host as a VM host and choose its interface (Hyper-V in 1.0)
HAW runs one fixed command on the host, vmctl, as an account that can do nothing else
Every VM on each host with its state, size, addresses and uptime
Start, resume, shut down, turn off and restart, with a confirm
The host keeps its own limits: a name pattern, a protect list and ceilings that HAW can't change
Open a VM's console in the Remote Desktop plugin
Three roles: owner, operator and viewer
A VM service other plugins (Runbooks) use to do VM actions for a person, for the plugins an admin allows
Every action recorded, in HAW and in Termix's audit log

gated.notes:
### Added

- **Resume a paused VM.** vmctl has a new verb, `resume`, for a VM that is paused. It is a power verb like `start`, for operators, and it works on a protected VM too. HAW has the route `POST /hosts/:id/vms/:name/resume`, recorded and audited as `resume`. A VM that is not paused gets `wrong-state`, and `start` on a paused VM now says to resume it instead.
- **VM status and drive space.** `list` and `show` give each VM's `status` (Hyper-V's own words for its health) and `critical` (Hyper-V marks the VM critical, as in Paused-Critical). `show` gives `drive`: the host drive that holds the VM's first disk file, with its size and free space in GB, or `null` for a share, a VM with no disk, or a drive that Windows does not measure.
- **Resume on the card.** A paused VM gets **Resume**, never **Start**, when the host's vmctl lists `resume`. Under its row, HAW shows Paused-Critical in words, Hyper-V's status and the free space of the VM's drive. Under 10 GB free, it adds "Hyper-V pauses a VM when its disk drive is almost full: free space first, then Resume." The details of every VM show the drive line.

### Changed

- **The VM service `haw.vms` is version 1.1.0.** It adds `resume(caller, host, name)`, with the same role rules as `start`, and the new `status`, `critical` and `drive` fields. The agent limit refuses `resume`. See [the VM service](docs/service.md).
- **The Hyper-V back end (`vmctl-worker.ps1`) is version 1.1.0.** `vmctl.ps1` and `install.ps1` did not change. HAW does not update a host by itself: run the host's setup of this version again (see [Update vmctl](docs/hyper-v.md#update-vmctl)). Until then, HAW works as before, without Resume, and says what to do for a paused VM.
- **Refresh updates the host's info.** After a host's vmctl is updated, its new verbs show when you press **Refresh**, without a reload of the page.

### Changed

- **One build for Termix 26.11.0 and 26.11.2 or later.** The manifest allows plugin API 1.13 and plugin API 2.9 (`"api": "^1.13 || ^2.9"`). On Termix 26.11.0, HAW runs as before. On Termix 26.11.2 or later, HAW runs in its own process and its tab in a sandboxed frame. HAW needs no `sandbox` block: it has no timers, event listeners or registry values of its own.
- HAW's icon is Lucide's **Trees** icon, the same drawing. Termix 26.11.2 draws only Lucide icons in the rail and on the tab; it showed a puzzle piece for the old icon.

### Fixed

- **The VM service binds under plugin API 2.** `bindPlugin` now waits for the consumer's receiver from `ctx.registry.consume`, which plugin API 2 gives as a Promise. Before, a plugin like Runbooks got `no-receiver` and could not use VM steps on Termix 26.11.2.

### Security

- **Termix API keys under plugin API 2.** Termix 26.11.2 and later do not tell a plugin process whether a request came in on a Termix API key (`tmx_...`), so HAW can't refuse API keys there as it does on Termix 26.11.0: a request with an admin's API key reaches HAW's routes as that admin. On Termix 26.11.0 nothing changes.

### Fixed

- **The queue's OWNER RIGHTS entry works.** `install.ps1` set the queue folder's owner after its entries, and Windows then drops the OWNER RIGHTS entry's "files" flag, so the entry did nothing: the vmctl account could change the access list of a request file it made. `install.ps1` now sets the owner first, and removes a dead entry before it grants the entry again. Run `install.ps1` once on each Hyper-V host to repair the queue.
- **`install.ps1` reports only real changes.** It reported SET for the queue access and the worker task on every run: the queue because of the dead entry, the task because Task Scheduler stores the account's "read and run" right as `0x1200a9`, not as the `GRGX` that `install.ps1` writes. It now compares the right as a number, so a second run ends with `CHANGED 0`.

### Added

- The VM service `haw.vms` (version 1.0.0), for other plugins: `hosts`, `info`, `list`, `show`, `start`, `stop`, `restart` and `consoleInfo`, as the acting person, with their HAW role and the host's limits, through the same vmctl call as the tab. Runbooks uses it for VM steps. See [the VM service](docs/service.md).
- **Plugins that may act for a person**, an admin setting: the plugin ids that may use the service, one a line. Empty by default.
- A plugin proves who it is with a key HAW hands to a receiver under the plugin's own id (`<id>.hawVmsKey`), as OpenBao Secrets' service does. Every call carries it.
- A call for an agent token (`agent: true`) may only list hosts and VMs.
- HAW's record keeps the plugin that acted for the person and its reference ("via runbooks: runbook 12 step 3"). **Record** and a VM's last action show it; Termix's audit line has it in its details.

### Changed

- A new VM list. Each VM is one item of two lines: its name with the Protected or Not-managed badge, then its state, size and addresses, with the uptime at the right. The buttons sit at the right and move under the name in a narrow pane, so the list never scrolls to the side.
- A click on a VM opens its details in place: generation, size, checkpoints and ID; each disk with its use; each network with its switch, MAC and addresses; the notes; and the last action HAW recorded on that VM. Turn off and Reset are in the details; the row keeps Start, Shut down, Restart and Console.
- On a phone, the rows have no buttons. The details show every button the VM allows, large, two to a line.
- Each host's header shows its VM count, its memory in use as a bar, and a **Limits** button for the name pattern, protect list and ceilings.
- A filter box (name or address) and **All**, **Running** and **Stopped** buttons with counts, above all hosts.

### Added

- `GET /actions` takes `vmName`, with `hostId`, for the last action on one VM.

### Changed

- The VM list keeps up by itself: while the tab is on screen, it reads each host's VMs again 2 seconds after the last read ended, so a VM that starts, stops or changes on the host shows without a click. A read never starts while another one or a power action is still running.

### Added

- VM hosts: any Termix host, with an interface (Hyper-V). **Add VM host** checks the host with `vmctl info` before it adds it, and shows that interface's one-time setup when vmctl does not answer. A host with no stored host key is refused.
- The vmctl protocol, version 1: one JSON request on standard input, one JSON reply. Verbs `info`, `list`, `show`, `start`, `stop`, `restart` and `console-info`; `create`, `delete`, `snapshot`, `restore` and `users` answer "not in this version".
- The Hyper-V back end, with `install.ps1` for the one-time setup. `vmctl.ps1` is the forced command of a plain account (key login, no TTY, no forwarding); it hands each request to the task `haw-vmctl-worker`, which runs `vmctl-worker.ps1` as SYSTEM, checks the request again and runs Hyper-V. Windows refuses Hyper-V to a non-admin account over an SSH key login, even in Hyper-V Administrators; the worker keeps the account out of Administrators. The host config holds a name pattern, a protect list and ceilings that the plugin can't change.
- A fake back end for tests and rehearsals (`vmctl/fake/vmctl-fake.mjs`).
- The VMs tab: each VM host with its VMs, state, size, addresses and uptime; Start, Shut down, Turn off, Restart and Reset with a confirm; protected and not-managed VMs marked.
- Consoles through the Remote Desktop plugin, from a Termix host an owner links to the VM.
- Roles: See VMs (viewer), Power VMs (operator) and Manage VM hosts (owner).
- The record of actions, in HAW's tables and in Termix's audit log.

plugins.name: OpenBao Secrets
plugins.description: Keep secrets in OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault, type them at a terminal's password prompt, and let other plugins store theirs.
plugins.author: Coolroo
features: One connection to OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault (KV v2), set up by an admin
The AppRole secret ID comes in a response-wrapped token and is never shown again
A Secrets tab for your own secrets and shared ones, by name, in folders
A saved value is never sent to the browser for display: no reveal, no copy
Type a secret at the cursor of an open terminal, for a password prompt
Put a secret in a shell variable, without showing it or saving it in history
A service other plugins use to store, read and delete secrets in their own area
Optional, off by default: other plugins may create (never read or replace) fields at app paths an admin allows
Secrets with an expiry time are deleted when it passes
Every read, write and delete is in the audit log, never with the value

gated.notes:
Ready for plugin API 2. This release still runs only on plugin API 1 (Termix 26.11.0 and 26.11.1) and works as 1.0.5 does there. The release for Termix 26.11.2 and later follows with the switch.

### Changed

- The icon is Lucide's **KeyRound** icon, the same drawing. Termix 26.11.2 draws only Lucide icons in the rail, on the tab, in the terminal toolbar and side panel, and in the command palette.
- The hourly expiry sweep has a schedule id (`expiry-sweep`), which plugin API 2 needs. Termix 26.11.0 ignores it.

### Fixed

- `bindPlugin` waits for the consumer's receiver from `ctx.registry.consume`, which plugin API 2 gives as a Promise. Without this, Runbooks and every other consumer would get "has no receiver" and no plugin area under plugin API 2.

### Added

- **App secrets**, off by default. The service `openbao-secrets.store` is now version 1.1.0, with `createAppField(caller, app, host, field, value)`: a plugin bound to the store adds one new field at `<app secrets folder>/<app>/<host>`, for another program that reads its secrets there. It never reads a value and never replaces a field: it reads the secret's field names (KV `subkeys`), refuses a field that exists, and writes with check-and-set (0 for a new secret, the checked version for a new field by JSON merge patch), trying once more after a lost race. A secret whose newest version is deleted or destroyed is refused.
- Admin settings **App secrets folder** (a folder in the KV mount, outside the base path) and **Allowed app paths** (one `<app>/<host>` per line). Both are empty by default, and the feature is off until both are set.
- The permission **Create app secrets** (`openbao-secrets.create-app-secrets`), for admins by default. Callers need it as well as **Use secrets**.
- An audit line for every try: the user, the calling plugin, the path and the field, never the value.
- Docs: the OpenBao policy lines for it (`create` and `patch` on data, `read` on `subkeys` and `metadata`), and what that policy cannot stop (a `patch` can replace a field; the plugin refuses to, the policy alone does not).

### Fixed

- The **Replace value** and **Delete** buttons on a secret's row are icons, as in Termix's own lists. They held words that spilled out of the buttons and over the row, most of all on a phone. Each icon keeps its name as a tooltip and for screen readers.

### Fixed

- **Add secret** and **Replace value** work with phone keyboards. An Android keyboard composes a whole word before it hands it over, and the old dots-only field missed those words, so **Add** stayed off. The value field is now a plain text field: typing, paste and autofill all set the value.

### Changed

- The value shows while you type, so you can check it before you save. A **Hide** button draws it as dots, and **Show** brings it back; neither changes the value. Once saved, a value is still never sent to the browser to be shown.

### Fixed

- Adding a secret when OpenBao accepts the value but refuses its metadata (for example a policy without create and update on the KV metadata path) no longer leaves the value behind with no expiry or creator. The new secret is taken back, and adding it again works once the policy is right.
